name: Dean Lukoye Atwoli sworn in as the chair of the board of Kenya's largest mental hospital

content.title: Dean Lukoye Atwoli sworn in as the chair of the board of Kenya's largest mental hospital
content.summary: Prof Atwoli has been actively involved in influencing policy in Kenya and on the continent

media.caption: Members of the Mathari National Teaching and Referral Hospital Board during the inauguration by CS for Health Mr Mutahi Kagwe
media.alt: Dean Lukoye Atwoli sworn in as the chair of the board of Kenya's largest mental hospital

content.text: Professor Lukoye Atwoli, Dean at the Medical College East Africa is the new chair of the Board of Kenya's largest mental hospital, the Mathari Teaching and Referral Hospital.

Together with four other board members who are leaders in their own right, Prof Lukoye Atwoli was sworn in by Kenya's Cabinet Secretary for Health, Hon Mutahi Kagwe. The other board members are Dr Sheetal Khanna, Ms Lena Munuve, Dr Frank Njenga (Presidential Advisor on Mental Health) and Maj (Rtd) Mike Kariuki. As is customary with most state corporations, additional members of the board are the Principal Secretaries in charge of health, correctional services, and finance.

Speaking at the inauguration, Prof Atwoli said: "Even if the mandate is to build the foundation so that others can come and build the walls and the roof, we will deliver on this mandate. We are passionate, we are determined, and we're going to do the job."

This latest appointment adds to many of his accolades and over one and a half decades of service to both academic and health institutions in Kenya and beyond. Other than being Dean of the Medical College at AKU, Prof Atwoli also holds visiting and honorary positions at the Harvard TH Chan School of Public Health and the University of Cape Town.

Over the past ten years, Prof Atwoli has been actively involved in influencing policy in Kenya and on the continent, as well as on the global scene. He has served as Vice-President of the Kenya Medical Association, and is currently the Secretary-General of the African Association of Psychiatrists and President-Elect of the African College of Neuropsychopharmacology. He serves on various committees of the World Psychiatric Association and the World Medical Association.

The Mathari Teaching and Referral Hospital in Nairobi is one of Kenya's oldest hospitals established in 1910. It is the only psychiatric hospital in the country and has a bed-capacity of 600. Prof Atwoli will lead the hospital board for the next three years.
